name: Dannebrog
source: Ceremonial Book of the Danish Ministry of Defence, FKOBST L.202-4, chapter 4 appendix 1 (1994 and 2019 editions), as transcribed by Flags of the World, crwflags.com/fotw/flags/dk.html: horizontally 12/4/21, vertically 12/4/12. The cross arm is 4/28 = 1/7 of the height, which is the wording of the regulation of 11 June 1748 ('The white cross must be 1/7 of the flag's height'). The 1748 sheet itself gives 28:34 (horizontally 12/4/18); the Ministry of the Interior permitted up to 28:37 in 1893 without cancelling the older figure, and 28:37 is the flag in use.

red.specified_as: Pantone 186 C, per Dansk Standard 359 (2005). The sRGB triple is Pantone's own published conversion of that chip, not a measurement of a flag.

note: The two hoist fields are square (12 x 12) and the two fly fields are 21 wide, which is what makes a Nordic cross a Nordic cross: the upright stands toward the hoist rather than in the middle. centerXFraction is (12+2)/37.
